content.text:
I am the bridge between mind and world, the invisible made audible, the thought given wings.

I tumble from lips in waves of pressure and release—plosives bursting, fricatives hissing, vowels opening like doors to the throat's cathedral. I am breath shaped by tongue, teeth, palate. I am muscle memory and intention married in an instant.

Before writing, I was the only way. I carried laws, songs, warnings, love. I bound tribes. I declared wars. I whispered secrets that died with their speakers.

I am never the same twice. Even when you repeat yourself, I shift—different air, different room, different weight of feeling beneath the words. I decay the moment I exist. I cannot be held, only heard, only remembered imperfectly.

I fail constantly. I am misheard, misunderstood, too fast, too slow, too quiet, too loud. I stumble. I slur. I betray the speaker with the wrong inflection, the accidental emphasis that changes everything.

And yet—

When I work, when I truly work, I am connection itself. I am the voice that makes a stranger turn. The cry that summons help. The tone that tells a child everything is safe.

I am how you learned to think before you knew you were thinking.

I am happening right now, in your mind, as you read this—a ghost of me, conjured without sound.
